To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the organic matter of several agricultural and industrial soils and sediments can be grossly fractionated into cellulose‐like, lignin‐like, lipid‐like, and humic substances‐like fractions; and that the sorption of the herbicide napropamide was greater in the soils than in the sediments on a dry weight basis, but greater in the sedimens than in the soils on an organic carbon or organic matter basis.
The organic matter of soils and sediments is composed of a wide variety of compounds.
soils and sediments contain different classes of organic matter that are not all equally important in sorption of nonionic pesticides.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an extraction procedure to fractionate organic matter in soils, sediments and aquatic humics and the determination of the contribution of these fractions to the sorption and degradation of pesticides.
the fractionation of organic matter in soil and sediment and the contribution of the various fractions to pesticide sorption.
the fractionation of the organic components of soil and sediments, and the effects of this fractionation on the sorption of nonionic pesticides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sorption of the test compound is not a function of a single organic fraction, but of a combination of fractions and their interactions with the mineral matrix.
the sorption behavior of the test chemical in soils and sedments is controlled by the organic carbon content and the type and quantity of specific organic compounds present.
the fractionation procedure used in this study was not successful in separating specific classes of organic matter from the soils and sediments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sorption of naprapamide on soils and sediments is not controlled solely by the organic carbon content of the sample.
the organic matter of soils and sediments is a complex and heterogeneous matrix and that the contribution of the various fractions to the sorption process is not readily predictable.
the sorption of the test compound was not affected by the removal of specific fractions, and that the effect of pH was more significant than the removal of specific organic matter fractions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sorption of organic chemicals is not only a function of the organic matter content of soils and sediments but is also affected by the nature of the organic matter present.

soils and sediments contain different classes of organic matter, that the sorption characteristics of the two materials differ significantly, and that removal of specific classes of organic matter can have a significant effect on the Koc of sediments but not soils.
the sorption of naprodimide on soils and sediments cannot be explained solely by their organic carbon content.
